chunks: And in the narration of Hishām ibn Sālim and Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

If the father and the grandfather both arrange the marriage, then the marriage arranged by the one who acted first takes precedence. But if they both arranged it at one and the same time, then the grandfather has greater authority.

key_terms.أَوْلَى: having greater right or stronger authority
key_terms.التَّزْوِيجُ: the act of marriage arrangement or marriage contract
key_terms.لِلْأَوَّلِ: for the one who acted first; indicating legal priority

ai.seo_question: If both the father and grandfather arrange a marriage, whose decision takes precedence?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about guardianship in marriage when both the father and the grandfather arrange a marriage. Priority belongs to the one who acted first, but if both acted simultaneously, the grandfather's authority takes precedence.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4393 - Hisham ibn Salim and Muhammad ibn Hakim narrated from Abu Abdullah (as) who said:

"If the father and the grandfather both arrange the marriage, the marriage arranged by the first one will take precedence. However, if both arranged the marriage simultaneously, then the grandfather has greater authority."
